# PRISMA2020 Checklist

As noted in *Materials and Methods*, "Literature Review Protocol", a systematic literature review framework was adapted from elements of PRISMA2020 [@pagePRISMA2020Statement2021]; as PRISMA2020 is primarily concerned with intervention-based studies, some elements were reinterpreted for an environmental exposure assessment. The checklist below follows the standard PRISMA2020 section structure. Each item's original wording is quoted from the project's internal literature review planning document, followed by where (if anywhere) it is currently addressed in this manuscript.

## Title

### Item 1: Title

*"(should include systematic review)"*

The manuscript title, "Copper Pollution in the Arctic - An Aggregate Exposure Pathway for Understanding Sources, Exposure, and Internal Concentrations", does not identify the work as a systematic review.

<!-- TODO (Sam): this looks like a deliberate framing choice (CLAUDE.md 4.5 -- scale in this paper comes from Vannmiljø, not the review, and AP01 should be reframed as targeted evidence-gathering rather than a systematic review) rather than an oversight. Confirm that's the intended read, or tell me how you'd like this line phrased. -->

## Abstract

### Item 2: Abstract

*"(See abstracts checklist)"*

The Abstract is a single ES&T-format paragraph (150-200 words, per the constraints noted in `_00-abstract.qmd`) and does not follow the separate PRISMA-for-abstracts structure (objectives, eligibility criteria, sources, risk of bias, included studies, synthesis, limitations, funding, registration) item by item.

## Introduction

### Item 3: Rationale

*"Describe the rationale for the review in the context of existing knowledge."*

Reported in the Introduction, opening two paragraphs (copper's ecological/economic significance; expected Arctic ecosystem change).

### Item 4: Objectives

*"Provide an explicit statement of the objective(s) or question(s) the review addresses."*

Reported in the Introduction, closing paragraph ("In this paper, we propose a conceptual AEP...").

### Item 8: Selection process

*"Specify the methods used to decide whether a study met the inclusion criteria of the review, including how many reviewers screened each record and each report retrieved, whether they worked independently, and if applicable, details of automation tools used in the process."*

Reported in *Materials and Methods*, "Literature Review Protocol" (de-duplication, abstract/full-text screening, 1-5 relevance ranking) and the accompanying flow diagram (@fig-prisma).

### Item 9: Data collection process

*"Specify the methods used to collect data from reports, including how many reviewers collected data from each report, whether they worked independently, any processes for obtaining or confirming data from study investigators, and if applicable, details of automation tools used in the process."*

Reported in *Materials and Methods*, "Data Extraction & Validation" (LLM-assisted extraction into the eData format, followed by review by one of three reviewers against the study text).

### Item 10a: Data items (outcomes)

*"List and define all outcomes for which data were sought. Specify whether all results that were compatible with each outcome domain in each study were sought, and if not, the methods used to decide which results to collect."*

Reported in *Materials and Methods*, "Data Extraction & Validation" and "Exposure Data Post-Processing" (concentration/dose data and associated metadata, structured to the eData schema).

### Item 13a-13f: Synthesis methods

*13a: "Describe the processes used to decide which studies were eligible for each synthesis." 13b: "Describe any methods required to prepare the data for presentation or synthesis, such as handling of missing summary statistics, or data conversions." 13c: "Describe any methods used to tabulate or visually display results of individual studies and syntheses." 13d: "Describe any methods used to synthesize results and provide a rationale for the choice(s). If meta-analysis was performed, describe the model(s), method(s) to identify the presence and extent of statistical heterogeneity, and software package(s) used." 13e: "Describe any methods used to explore possible causes of heterogeneity among study results." 13f: "Describe any sensitivity analyses conducted to assess robustness of the synthesized results."*

13a/13b/13c are reported in *Materials and Methods*, "Exposure Data Post-Processing" and "AEP Construction" (grouping, unit standardisation, and tabulation into sample groups and AEP nodes).
